title: About the Centre
text:
The Centre for Household Finance is a research centre in the Department of Economics at Stellenbosch University. Our goal is to advance knowledge about consumer financial markets in developing countries: how they work, and which policies may make them work more efficiently and more equitably.
We use tools from applied microeconomics and causal inference to study how people make financial decisions and what influences their choices. We focus on South African survey and administrative data across a range of domains, including retirement, insurance and credit.

title: Centre for Household Finance
text:
We are a research group within the Department of Economics at Stellenbosch University. Our goal is to advance knowledge about consumer financial markets in developing countries, and South Africa in particular: how they work, and which policies may make them work more efficiently and more equitably.
We use tools from applied microeconomics and causal inference to study how people make financial decisions and what influences their choices. We focus on South African survey and administrative data in a variety of domains, including retirement, insurance, and credit.

title: Research
text: We use tools from applied microeconomics and causal inference to study how South African households make financial decisions, and which policies would make consumer financial markets work more efficiently and more equitably.

title: Research
text:
Research programmes
Our work is organised into programmes. Each output below is tagged with the programme it belongs to; use the tags to filter the list.
Mortgage pricing in South Africa. Access to affordable housing finance is essential for economic mobility, yet mortgage pricing varies significantly across applicants. This programme investigates disparities in mortgage offer probabilities and interest rates by age, gender, marital status and first-time buyer status, with a view to policies that promote fair and transparent lending.
The market for funeral insurance. Funeral insurance is one of the most widely purchased financial products in South Africa, while life insurance remains far less common. This programme examines the extent to which the two are substitutes, on both the supply side — regulatory barriers and industry practice — and the demand side, where mortality, income and intergenerational living arrangements shape what households buy.
